entities.summary: Karl Friedrich August Gützlaff, anglicised as Charles Gutzlaff, was a German Lutheran missionary to the Far East, notable as one of the first Protestant missionaries in Bangkok, Thailand (1828) and the first Lutheran missionary to China (1831-1848). He was a colorful "swashbuckling Pomeranian" who combined his prodigious talent as a prolific Christian author and linguist with participation in the illegal opium trade in 1830s China. He was one of the first Protestant missionaries in China to dress in Chinese clothing and was said to be so proficient in Chinese language and culture that he could pass as Chinese.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As one of the first Protestant missionaries in China and a key figure in the introduction of Western Christianity to East Asia, Gützlaff played a significant role in shaping regional religious dynamics. His linguistic and cultural expertise allowed him to navigate complex Chinese society, influencing the trajectory of Christian missions in the region.
